rubrics.justification: Accurately describes an expanded/early-hatching blastocyst with plausible B-grade ICM and strong TE, notes thinned zona and limitation of static image; minor uncertainty around 4 vs 5 stage prevents a perfect score.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and patient factors; minor issue in presenting implantation and clinical pregnancy ranges that slightly overlap inconsistently.

Recommendations are largely consistent with Gardner grading, single embryo transfer in a good-prognosis 31-year-old, and cautious stance on PGT-A; slight overreach in some lifestyle advice and probability framing keeps it from perfect.
Provides clear, practical next steps for current transfer, luteal support, lifestyle, and contingency planning after failure, including when to avoid over-investigation and what to review.
